quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even when you signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: What should you do when a railroad crossing gate is lowering?

options.text: Speed up and cross before the gate closes completely.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when the gate is lowering. It is unsafe to do anything else.

questions.question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?

options.text: Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.

questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes ahead. Look for signals from other drivers. Watch for vehicles merging at on-ramps and be ready for quick changes in road conditions and traffic.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is not enough room on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
When the railroad crossing is in a city or town with frequent trains.
When you are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is not enough room on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time from either direction. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you can no longer see the other vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane. Always check your blind spots first.

questions.question: As daylight fades, what lights should you use to help others see you?
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades. Use high beams only when no other drivers are nearby.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign means a steep hill is ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to protect your brakes.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level increases, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. The higher the BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed near schools to warn drivers to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: It is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means it is illegal to pass in that area. You are likely in an area with poor visibility where passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: Before turning on the engine, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Before starting your car, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: How can drivers prevent eye fatigue when driving at night?

options.text: Keep moving your eyes and scan the road.
Close your eyes for a few seconds at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving your eyes and scan the road.
questions.explanation: Night driving causes eye fatigue. Move your eyes from the center of the road to the sides and from near to far ahead to stay alert.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children have slower reflexes than adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see than adults.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Children on bikes may suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: When must vehicles stop behind a school bus with red lights flashing?

options.text: Until all students leave the bus.
Until the stop arm is raised.
Until the stop arm is raised and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Until the stop arm is raised and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stop until the red lights are off, the stop arm is raised, and the bus starts moving again.

questions.question: When bad weather makes it hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: In darkness or bad weather, stay farther behind the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to hazards you may not see.

questions.question: This sign is a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: Triangle-shaped signs pointing downward mean yield. Slow down and stop if necessary. Stop at a marked stop line if one exists.

questions.question: In rain or fog, what lights should drivers use?
questions.explanation: Use low beams in rain or fog. While they may not help you see much more, they help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and go with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What is the law about posters and signs on car windows?

options.text: They are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.
They are illegal if they block the driver's view of the road.
They are allowed if they do not contain offensive language.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are illegal if they block the driver's view of the road.
questions.explanation: State law prohibits anything on windows that blocks the driver's clear view of the road.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a red traffic signal?

options.text: Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Drive through the intersection without stopping.

questions.explanation: Stop at a red traffic signal. Stay stopped until the light turns green.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your reactions and decision-making. You could fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting yourself or others.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones and be ready to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. No passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It also makes it harder to see clearly and judge distances and speeds.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How do you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a constant speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on a wet road. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent it.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Make speed and direction changes slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and direction changes slowly.
questions.explanation: Make all speed and direction changes gradually on snow or ice. Never use cruise control because your tires may lose contact with the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Your car breaks down on the highway. What should you do?

options.text: Park with all four wheels off the road, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down, park with all four wheels off the main part of the road if possible.

questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:
questions.explanation: You need more time and distance to stop on a slippery road. Keep a greater distance from the car ahead on slippery roads.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at crashes or unusual things:
questions.explanation: Avoid slowing down to look at crashes. This helps keep traffic moving.

questions.question: How can you help the car behind you stay a safe distance away?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.

questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and signal your turns and lane changes in advance. This helps the car behind you stay a safe distance away.

questions.question: When you see an octagonal sign, you must:
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means "Stop." Come to a complete stop, let traffic and pedestrians pass, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep downgrade ahead. Check your brakes.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to clear the area.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians. If you see them near the road, slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You often see it at intersections with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop. On one-way streets, drive toward the nearest edge.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speeds require greater following distance.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 mph, survival is unlikely. Higher speeds also require longer stopping distances, so you need more following distance.
